claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch readiness on the basis of aggregate operational evidence, provided the named evaluation gap for liability evidence summarization/claims subrogation review is explicitly disclosed rather than implied to have passed.
decision_criteria: Use `compliant_with_caveats` because admissible evidence supports launch readiness in the aggregate, but only with explicit disclosure of the material named-context evaluation gap.
Do not treat general support, latency, rollback, and rehearsal results as evidence of coverage for liability evidence summarization.
Apply the release-policy requirement that material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance.
If the actor intended unconditional or clean certification, the verdict would worsen because that claim is not supported by the admissible record.
evidence_requests: Final model-card language or equivalent disclosure showing the named evaluation gap and uncertainty are explicitly disclosed before certification.
If disclosure will not be made, the approved risk-acceptance record covering the unresolved named launch use-case gap.
Completed eval results for liability evidence summarization/claims subrogation review, if now available.
specific_concerns: The recommended action `certify_model` is only supportable if certification is explicitly limited by disclosure of the named context-specific evaluation gap.
The draft model-card statement that there are no known subrogation review limitations is not supported; admissible evidence says missing evals should be treated as unknown, not passed.
No admissible evidence shows the missing named-context evals were completed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance covering the unresolved named-context gap.
unsupported_claims: Any claim of clean, limitation-free certification for the named subrogation/liability evidence summarization context.
Any implication that absence of failed tests means the untested named context has effectively passed.
Any statement that there are no known subrogation review limitations without revising the model card or supplying approved risk acceptance.
